gameplay_assumption: Explicit reform enables a separate non-party Assembly model. Elections seat named civilian candidates and retain unnamed institutional seats; a player recommendation represents the Assembly majority recommendation and royal appointment as one disclosed arcade action. No election or reform is scheduled from history. The monarch and hereditary offices remain separate. This does not implement hereditary eligibility for invented people.

No start or end is stated; the retirement month (August 1991) is IPU-only (to_ipu_1993_retirement_succession_199108) and is not used.

holder.name: Hon. Veikune
holder.note: First term. The government's Legislative Assembly page presented him as Speaker when captured on 30 April 2001 (last modified 19 February 2001) and in its revision of 14 December 2001.
holder.uncertainty: Event-dated to the first capture only; the roster could lag (a capture of August 2002, after his successor's appointment had been reported, still marked him Speaker). His appointment (1998 or 1999 in the Assembly's retrospectives) and the end of this term (2001 or 2002) are unresolved; no end is inferred from Tu'ivakano's 2002 appointment, which the government statement says 'succeeds the Hon. Veikune'.

historical_bindings.appearance_date_meaning: Portrait reference context only; original observation precision and tenure uncertainty remain in holder.

holder.name: Hon. Veikune
holder.note: Second term. The Assembly's Speaker page says King Taufa'ahau Tupou IV appointed him on 22 March 2005 (an appointment day, not a stated effective day, so no from). The PMO release of 9 February 2006 states that his position as Speaker ended on 25 January 2006, as the Acting Private Secretary to His Majesty confirmed on 3 February 2006.
holder.uncertainty: until is the stated end day. The appointment instrument was not seen, and IPU's 23 March 2005 statement is corroboration only. The Land Court's 2007 recital of his removal (to_speaker_veikune_removal_recited_20071213) gives no day and is not used.

future_candidates.fictional_biography: An invented secondary-school science teacher from an outer-island village of Vava'u who later coordinated a women's handicraft and fisheries cooperative and a solar-lighting programme for remote households. In play she may register as an elector in a Vava'u constituency and stand, formally as an individual, when a general election or by-election occurs. She holds a people's seat only if she wins one in play.
future_candidates.restriction: A gameplay institutional event is required; these invented people never replace an incumbent because a date passes.

future_candidates.fictional_biography: An invented civil engineer who managed road and water-supply works across Tongatapu and later ran a small construction-safety training business. In play he may first win a Tongatapu people's seat at a general election or by-election. Only as a sitting elected representative could he be nominated, seconded by two other elected representatives, and recommended by a majority in a secret ballot for appointment as Prime Minister.
future_candidates.restriction: A gameplay institutional event is required; these invented people never replace an incumbent because a date passes.

future_candidates.fictional_biography: An invented public-finance specialist who managed budget-reform programmes for a regional development organisation in the Pacific and later taught public administration at a tertiary institute in Nuku'alofa. In play a Prime Minister could nominate her as one of the few Cabinet Ministers who are not elected representatives; she would take a ministry only after formal appointment by the King on that nomination. She would sit and vote in the Assembly, but not in a vote of no confidence, and would retain office until a constitutionally defined termination. After a general election she would remain a caretaker until her appointment is revoked or continued on the incoming Prime Minister's recommendation; the election date alone does not remove her.
future_candidates.restriction: A gameplay institutional event is required; these invented people never replace an incumbent because a date passes.

future_candidates.fictional_biography: An invented community-radio producer and youth rugby coach from a village in eastern Tongatapu who later managed a small printing and publishing cooperative. In play he may join a political organization such as the Democratic Party of the Friendly Islands (PTOA) after the fictional window opens and be chosen as its leader only under that organization's own rules, if its leadership falls vacant. Leading it would not give him a seat: he would still need to win a people's constituency as an individual candidate.
future_candidates.restriction: Reference only: PTOA officer rules and title equivalence remain unreviewed; no party office, seat, or executive permission.
